I see I got pinged a lot on this, it's better to cc @berarma , who was responsible for #101958. I don't know anything about Theora other than how to use the encoder effectively.

Also I don't see how having support for recording in such a legacy format is beneficial. If there is something worth to be spending time on, it would be enabling MovieWriter to pipe to FFmpeg. It would close a lot of [these proposals](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues?q=sort%3Aupdated-desc%20is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20ffmpeg), directly or indirectly. Just my two cents.

A reminder that Windows 64bits has assembler optimizations disabled due to issues with register allocation, so it might run slower there.

```
ERROR: Couldn't set encoder flags for soft-target.
   at: write_begin (servers/movie_writer/movie_writer_ogv.cpp:245)
ERROR: Couldn't set rate control buffer for soft-target.
   at: write_begin (servers/movie_writer/movie_writer_ogv.cpp:256)
```

The reason for these errors is that there's no target bitrate set (it's zero). They are only valid when there's a target bitrate. I think these parameters can be ignored, the code removed, and the problem would be solved.

The keyframe errors have another cause. Please, see my code reviews, that might fix it.

I don't have experimented much with encoding parameters apart from the GOP and quality settings. I would leave GOP and video/audio quality as settings, and maybe `speed` in case it has a noticeable impact. For any other parameters use the library defaults.

I've done a couple of tests with `speed` and the default value 1 is actually faster than 4 on my computer, I'm not sure why. It's ~0.80ms/frame with speed=4 and ~0.60ms/frame with speed=1.

Higher values remove features. I would leave the default library setting removing the code that changes it. Unless someone gets different results, in which case I would add a setting for it.

> I've done a couple of tests with speed and the default value 1 is actually faster than 4 on my computer, I'm not sure why. It's ~0.80ms/frame with speed=4 and ~0.60ms/frame with speed=1.

I've tried to change `speed` to `1` and it seems very slightly faster, while the resulting OGV file is 3 KB smaller (for a 112 MB file). I've tested with an optimized build this time; I've updated the figures in OP.

I've done some tests using `theora_encode_example` with the same options used in this PR and changing speed values

I haven't found any case where speed=1 was faster than speed=4 so maybe I did something wrong.

I have done more tests and I've identified several issues that, while not too serious, can produce incorrect or suboptimal video files.

The code has been copied from [encoder_example](https://gitlab.xiph.org/xiph/theora/-/blob/master/examples/encoder_example.c) and while it produces valid video and audio streams, the multiplexing of these streams into an OGV file is incorrect.

The issues I've found:

- As reviewed above, some pages can be lost if we don't request them all in a loop.
- Unbalanced interleaving of video/audio pages, specially when there's no audio (silence) and consequently the audio stream is highly compressed. It can result in higher memory usage (buffering) and latency when decoding.
- Incorrect ordering of pages in the Ogg container. This is against the spec and could introduce issues when decoding and seeking.
- The video stream doesn't signal the end of the stream. This is probably innocuous.

The error `[ffmpeg/demuxer] ogg: Broken file, keyframe not correctly marked.` isn't really an error in the video file but probably in FFmpeg. It expects keyframes to be in its own page and shows this error when a keyframe shares the page with other non-keyframes. This is probably desirable but not required.

In my tests, this PR can produce videos significantly smaller than the AVI/MJPEG format in the same time (debug build), probably CPU dependent when seeing your results. Even smaller if we don't mind that the encoding takes almost double the time.

@Calinou, I can work on this if you're interested. There will be a lot of changes to do to `movie_writer_ogv.cpp`. What would be the best way to commit these changes? There are other pending issues that may take a bit to fix so maybe you prefer to wait.
